eng_translation: Adenocarcinoma is a type of cancer that originates in glandular tissue. It is characterized by the uncontrolled growth of abnormal cells that form tumors, often arising from epithelial cells that line internal organs or glands. Adenocarcinomas can occur in various parts of the body, including the lungs, breasts, colon, pancreas, and prostate. The diagnosis is typically made through histopathological examination of biopsy samples, and treatment options depend on the location, stage, and grade of the tumor. Common symptoms may include localized pain, changes in bowel or bladder habits, unexplained weight loss, and fatigue. Early detection and appropriate treatment are crucial for improving prognosis.
